description: Curated solutions knowledge base for the Talaix Solutions Intelligence engine (docs/SOLUTIONS_INTELLIGENCE.md). This is REFERENCE KNOWLEDGE about generic solution CLASSES — not products, not vendors, not observations. Every entry carries applicability conditions the engine checks against real site values, stated limitations, and real citable sources (organisation + URL). No entry quantifies benefits or costs unless a documented public figure exists; cost_basis is 'not quantified' by default. Species-level vegetation detail lives in config/species_knowledge.json and is referenced, not duplicated.

solution_classes.technology: Sensing, monitoring, data and automation approaches
solution_classes.water_management: Water storage, conservation and drainage approaches

applicability_fields.climate_zones: list of site climate zones the solution fits (null = unconstrained)
applicability_fields.min_elevation_m: minimum site elevation in metres (null = unconstrained)
applicability_fields.max_elevation_m: maximum site elevation in metres (null = unconstrained)
applicability_fields.moisture_regimes: list of site moisture regimes the solution fits (null = unconstrained)
applicability_fields.landcover_any: at least one of these ESA WorldCover class labels must be present on site (null = unconstrained)
applicability_fields.requires_water: true = mapped surface-water features must be present on site
applicability_fields.requires_urban: true = a mapped urban/building presence is required (>= 20 mapped buildings, matching the exposure layer's 'moderate' threshold)

solutions.name: Fuel management (thinning, clearing, fuel breaks)
solutions.mechanism: Reduces fuel load and horizontal/vertical fuel continuity so fire intensity and rate of spread drop; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: requires repeated maintenance — fuel regrows
can conflict with habitat protection goals
ineffective as sole measure under extreme fire weather
environmental_considerations: habitat effects to assess per site

sources.name: NFPA Firewise USA
UNEP — Spreading like Wildfire: The Rising Threat of Extraordinary Landscape Fires

solutions.name: Fire-resistant landscape design around assets
solutions.mechanism: Low-flammability, well-spaced vegetation and managed zones near structures reduce ember ignition and flame contact; species selection is guided by the curated species knowledge base (config/species_knowledge.json). Benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: no vegetation is fireproof
requires ongoing upkeep of defensible space
does not address crown-fire behaviour in surrounding wildland
environmental_considerations: water use of landscaping to assess in dry regions

sources.name: NFPA Firewise USA
EUFORGEN — European Forest Genetic Resources Programme

solutions.name: Wildfire detection and monitoring (satellite + ground)
solutions.mechanism: Earlier detection shortens response time; combines satellite active-fire detections and fire-danger forecasting with ground observation. Benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: depends on response capacity; not quantifiable site-generically

limitations: detection does not equal suppression capacity
satellite revisit and cloud cover limit timeliness
false alarms possible
solutions.maintenance: low-medium; service subscriptions and sensor upkeep

sources.name: EFFIS — European Forest Fire Information System
NASA FIRMS — Fire Information for Resource Management System

solutions.name: Water-point resilience for suppression and drought buffering
solutions.mechanism: Secured, accessible water storage points support fire suppression and buffer dry spells; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: depends on network design and local hydrology study

limitations: requires hydrological assessment
evaporation losses in hot dry climates
access must be designed and maintained
environmental_considerations: can provide habitat if designed accordingly

sources.name: FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization (water and land programmes)
UNEP — Spreading like Wildfire: The Rising Threat of Extraordinary Landscape Fires

solutions.name: Wetland restoration & flood retention
solutions.mechanism: Temporarily stores peak flows and releases water slowly, buffering both floods and dry periods; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: requires land availability
multi-year establishment
retention capacity is finite and site-specific

sources.name: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands
UNEP — United Nations Environment Programme

solutions.name: Engineered flood retention and detention basins
solutions.mechanism: Engineered storage intercepts and delays runoff peaks; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: land take
failure risk must be engineered and inspected
sedimentation reduces capacity over time

sources.name: European Commission — Floods Directive (EU water policy)
UNDRR — United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

solutions.name: Sustainable urban drainage (SUDS) and urban green infrastructure
solutions.mechanism: Permeable surfaces, swales and urban greening retain stormwater locally and cool the urban microclimate; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: limited capacity in extreme events
retrofitting dense urban areas is constrained
requires space allocation

sources.name: European Environment Agency — urban adaptation
European Commission — Environment (water and green infrastructure)

solutions.name: Flood early warning (discharge-based forecasting and alerting)
solutions.mechanism: Hydrological forecasting and alerting buys preparation time ahead of high-discharge events; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: value depends on local preparedness and response plans

limitations: forecast skill limited for flash floods
alerts only help where response plans exist
model resolution may miss small catchments

sources.name: GloFAS — Global Flood Awareness System (Copernicus EMS)
United Nations — Early Warnings for All

solutions.name: Water conservation and demand management
solutions.mechanism: Reduces demand and losses so available supplies last longer through dry periods; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: behavioural and governance dependent
savings saturate
does not create new supply

sources.name: European Environment Agency — water resources and scarcity
FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization

solutions.name: Smart / deficit irrigation scheduling
solutions.mechanism: Soil-moisture and weather-informed scheduling applies water only when and where crops need it; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: requires sensors, connectivity and skills
savings vary by crop and soil
upfront equipment cost (not quantified here)

sources.name: FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization (irrigation and water management)

solutions.name: Drought-tolerant species and variety selection
solutions.mechanism: Species and varieties with documented drought tolerance maintain cover and yield with less water; species-level guidance lives in the curated species knowledge base (config/species_knowledge.json). Benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: local trials and agronomic advice required

limitations: tolerance is not immunity — severe drought still damages
establishment phase still needs water
species choice must be verified locally
environmental_considerations: prefer locally native or non-invasive species
biodiversity effects of monocultures to avoid

sources.name: EUFORGEN — European Forest Genetic Resources Programme
FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization

solutions.name: Soil-moisture monitoring for drought early detection
solutions.mechanism: Combines reanalysis/satellite soil-moisture products with in-situ sensors to detect developing soil drought early; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: value depends on the decisions the monitoring informs

limitations: satellite products are top-layer and coarse-resolution
in-situ sensors need maintenance
monitoring alone saves no water

sources.name: Copernicus Climate Data Store (ERA5-Land soil moisture)

solutions.name: Urban green and blue cooling (trees, parks, water features)
solutions.mechanism: Shade and evapotranspiration lower surface and air temperatures locally; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: microclimate modelling or measurement required per site

limitations: trees take years to reach effective canopy
irrigation demand in dry climates
cooling effect is local, not city-wide by default
environmental_considerations: species choice must suit future climate

sources.name: European Environment Agency — urban adaptation to climate change
US EPA — Heat Island Reduction Program

solutions.name: Shading structures and cool / reflective materials
solutions.mechanism: Shade and high-albedo surfaces reduce absorbed solar radiation on streets and buildings; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: does not address night-time heat storage alone
material durability and glare to assess
winter-time penalties possible in cold climates

sources.name: US EPA — Heat Island Reduction Program

solutions.name: Heat-health warning and action plans
solutions.mechanism: Forecast-triggered alerts and pre-agreed actions protect vulnerable people during heat events; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: requires health-system and civil-protection coordination
alert fatigue
does not reduce the hazard itself

sources.name: WHO — heatwaves and health
WMO — World Meteorological Organization

solutions.name: Shelterbelts and windbreaks
solutions.mechanism: Tree/shrub rows reduce near-ground wind speed, limiting crop damage, evapotranspiration losses and soil erosion; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: depends on design and orientation vs prevailing wind

limitations: takes land out of production
multi-year establishment
wrong design can increase turbulence
environmental_considerations: species must suit local water availability

sources.name: FAO — Food and Agriculture Organization (agroforestry)

solutions.name: Wind-resistant design and retrofit of buildings
solutions.mechanism: Code-based wind-load design, roof-to-wall connections and opening protection reduce structural damage; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: retrofit costs per building (not quantified here)
does not protect against debris from surroundings
enforcement quality matters

sources.name: UNDRR — United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

solutions.name: Hazard-aware siting of new infrastructure
solutions.mechanism: Locating new assets outside documented hazard footprints — including documented seismicity zones (USGS ComCat seismic context) — avoids exposure rather than defending against it; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: avoided-loss accounting requires a documented valuation method — not integrated

limitations: only applies to new development
land-use planning authority required
hazard footprints have uncertainty
environmental_considerations: can steer development away from sensitive ecosystems

sources.name: UNDRR — United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
IPCC — Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change

solutions.name: Dune restoration and management
solutions.mechanism: Vegetated dune systems dissipate wave and wind energy and store sand that buffers storm erosion; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: only applicable on sandy coasts
vulnerable to trampling and development pressure
does not stop long-term shoreline retreat under sea-level rise
solutions.maintenance: low-medium; fencing, planting and access management

sources.name: UNEP — United Nations Environment Programme
IPCC — Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change

solutions.name: Coastal wetland and saltmarsh restoration
solutions.mechanism: Intertidal vegetation attenuates waves and storm surge before they reach assets; benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: requires suitable intertidal space
multi-year establishment
limited effect in extreme surge events

sources.name: Ramsar Convention on Wetlands
UNEP — United Nations Environment Programme

solutions.name: Coastal monitoring and storm-surge early warning
solutions.mechanism: Ocean forecasting and sea-level monitoring give lead time before surge and erosion events; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: value depends on preparedness and response plans

limitations: forecast uncertainty near complex coastlines
alerting requires response plans
does not reduce the hazard itself

sources.name: Copernicus Marine Service
United Nations — Early Warnings for All

solutions.name: Dust / sandstorm monitoring and early warning
solutions.mechanism: Dust transport monitoring and forecast-based warning give lead time for transport, solar-energy and outdoor-activity decisions; benefit declared qualitative.

expected_benefit.quantification_note: value depends on the decisions the warnings inform

limitations: detection/forecast skill varies by region and model
warning does not reduce the hazard itself
regional dust terminology must not be merged across sources

sources.name: WMO SDS-WAS — Sand and Dust Storm Warning Advisory and Assessment System (Barcelona Dust Centre)
CAMS — Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service

solutions.name: Volcanic activity monitoring and preparedness planning
solutions.mechanism: Authoritative volcano observatories and the Global Volcanism Program document activity and history; preparedness planning uses that documented evidence. Benefit declared qualitative.
limitations: eruption timing cannot be predicted by this class of tool
coverage depends on observatory networks
documented history is not a forecast

sources.name: Smithsonian Institution / USGS — Global Volcanism Program

knowledge_curation.source_verification: All source URLs were resolve-checked on 2026-08-18: 18/20 returned HTTP 200 to automated clients; ramsar.org and the UNEP report deep-link return 403 to automated clients (bot protection) — both are canonical institutional addresses that load in normal browsers.
knowledge_curation.source_license_note: Each source is governed by its provider's terms; consult the linked page. Talaix stores no source content, only references.
knowledge_curation.quantification_note: No entry quantifies benefits or costs today; quantification_status is 'not_quantified' on every entry by deliberate policy until a documented public figure with method and context exists.

solution_packages.name: Wildfire resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Detection shortens response time, fuel management reduces fire intensity and spread, asset-level landscaping reduces structure ignition, and secured water points support suppression — the components address different stages (early warning, hazard reduction, asset protection, response support), so they combine rather than overlap.

solution_packages.name: Flood resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Early warning buys preparation time, retention and wetlands store and slow peak flows, urban drainage handles local stormwater, and hazard-aware siting avoids new exposure — warning, storage, absorption, drainage and avoidance address different parts of the flood problem.

solution_packages.name: Drought resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Monitoring detects developing soil drought early, conservation reduces demand, irrigation scheduling applies scarce water precisely, tolerant species lower baseline water need, and water points buffer dry spells — detection, demand reduction, efficiency, resistance and buffering are complementary layers.

solution_packages.name: Urban heat resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Alerting protects vulnerable people during events while green/blue cooling and shading/cool materials reduce urban heat load between events — immediate protection combined with long-term exposure reduction.

solution_packages.name: Wind resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Windbreaks reduce near-ground wind over productive land, wind-resistant construction reduces structural damage, and hazard-aware siting keeps new assets out of the most exposed locations — landscape, asset and planning scales combined.

solution_packages.name: Coastal resilience package
solution_packages.why_together: Monitoring and surge warning give lead time, dunes and coastal wetlands dissipate wave and surge energy, and hazard-aware siting avoids new exposure — warning, natural buffers and avoidance address different time horizons of coastal risk.
